TINGNAN: Pamamahagi ng Emergency Shelter Assistance (ESA) | Disyembre 28, 2025

Bilang agarang pagtugon sa insidente ng sunog na naganap noong ika-27 ng Disyembre 2025 sa Barangay Matadero, Cabanatuan City, animnapu’t tatlong (63) pamilyang apektado ang nabigyan ng Emergency Shelter Assistance (ESA) na nagkakahalagang ₱10,000.00 bawat pamilya, mula sa City Government of Cabanatuan, sa pangunguna ng City Social Welfare and Development Office (CSWDO).

Ang pamamahagi ay isinagawa sa Plaza Lucero, Cabanatuan City, sa pamumuno ng ating butihing Punong Lungsod Myca Elizabeth R. Vergara at pakikipagtulungan ng staff ng CSWDO sa pangunguna ni Gng. Helen S. Bagasao. Bukod sa cash assistance, bawat benepisyaryong pamilya ay nabigyan din ng DSWD Relief Supplies, 25 kilo ng bigas, hygiene kits at sleeping kits upang matugunan ang kanilang agarang pangangailangan.

Ilan sa mga pamilyang naapektuhan ay patuloy na namamalagi sa entablado (stage) ng Plaza Lucero, na kasalukuyang nagsisilbing pansamantalang tirahan habang isinasagawa ang karagdagang assessment at koordinasyon para sa susunod na hakbang ng tulong.

Patuloy ang Pamahalaang Lungsod ng Cabanatuan at ang CSWDO sa pagsasagawa ng mga kinakailangang interbensyon upang matiyak ang maayos, sistematiko, at napapanahong tulong para sa mga pamilyang naapektuhan ng kalamidad, kasabay ng pasasalamat sa lahat ng ahensyang katuwang sa agarang pagtugon.

PABATID

Alinsunod sa Republic Act No. 7183 o Firecracker Law, ang pagbebenta, pamamahagi, at paggawa ng mga paputok at pailaw ay mahigpit na binabantayan ng pamahalaan.

Ayon rin sa City Ordinance no. 2010-038 (Revised Revenue Code), ang pagtitinda ng Firecrackers at Pyrotechnic Devices ay nangangailangan ng mga sumusunod: 

- Fire Safety Inspection Certificate mula sa Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP)
- DTI Registration (para sa single proprietorship)
- Permit to Sell Firecrackers and Pyrotechnic Devices issued by Philippine National Police (PNP)
- Fireworks Safety Training Course Certificate issue by Philippine National Police (PNP)
- Certification of Authority as retailer from the dealer of Fire Works 
- Photocopy of the Manufacturer's Dealer's License
- Barangay Clearance
- Market Clearance mula sa opisina ng  CEEPUMO

Kung mayroon man pong hindi napahintulutang magtinda, maaring sila ay hindi nakasunod sa mga nasabing alituntunin. 

Ang pagsunod sa batas at pakikipagtulungan ay para sa kaligtasan ng lahat.

Hazel Anne C. Pascual is a Year 10 student at the Nueva Ecija University of Science and Technology, where her growing passion for the visual arts continues to shine. From an early age, Hazel has been drawn to the world of painting and drawing, finding comfort, expression, and purpose in every stroke of her brush and pencil. Her artistic journey is deeply rooted in her fascination with people, which is why the majority of her works center on portraiture.

Hazel's portraits often capture more than just physical likeness they reflect emotion, character, and the subtle stories hidden within a person's gaze. She strives to bring life and depth to each piece, blending technical precision with her own unique sense of style and sensitivity. Her attention to detail and dedication to improvement demonstrate a maturity beyond her years, making her a promising young artist within her community.

As she continues to explore different techniques and mediums, Hazel remains inspired by the beauty of human expression and the endless possibilities of visual storytelling. With each new artwork, she further develops her artistic voice and moves closer to carving her place in the world of portrait art.

As part of the Marcos Administration’s initiative to improve the lives of farmers in Central Luzon, the Department of Agriculture, through the Philippine Center for Postharvest Development and Mechanization (PHilMech) and the Regional Field Office in Central Luzon (DA-RFO3), today provided various forms of assistance to farmer-beneficiaries in the 3rd District of Nueva Ecija.
 
A total of 44 farmers’ cooperatives and associations (FCAs) received aid primarily in the form of farm equipment and hybrid rice seeds, just in time for the 2025-2026 dry cropping season.
 
Leading the list of interventions are 33 farm tractors valued at Php78.99 million, funded under the Rice Competitiveness Enhancement Fund - Mechanization Program 2.0. Additionally, three mechanical planters worth Php1.35 million, five farm tractors totaling Php8 million, one combine harvester priced at Php1.8 million, and two hand tractors worth Php360,000 were distributed, all funded under the DA Rice and Corn programs, bringing the total to Php90.50 million.
 
Also provided were 22,103 bags of hybrid seeds valued at Php110.51 million, 22,103 bags of fertilizer amounting to Php17.41 million, 44,206 liters of liquid foliar valued at Php34.83 million, and 22.10 kilograms of powder foliar worth Php17.417 million. These contributions from DA-RFO3 total Php180.18 million.
 
DA Secretary Francisco P. Tiu Laurel and House Speaker Faustino "Bojie" De Guzman Dy III led the distribution of certificates of award to the farmer beneficiaries.

President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. today, December 10, 2025, led the groundbreaking ceremony for a 20-hectare Korea Agricultural Machinery Industry Complex (KAMIC) in Cabanatuan City, marking a significant step in his administration's efforts to usher in industrialization and economic development in the countryside.
 
“The Philippine Center for Postharvest Development and Mechanization (PHilMech) has been planning this initiative for nearly 10 years. The first step was the establishment of the country’s first Agricultural Machinery Design and Prototyping Center (AMDPC), which was inaugurated on December 7, 2023, at the PHilMech headquarters in Muñoz, Nueva Ecija, by Agriculture Secretary Francisco Tiu Laurel, Jr.,” said PHilMech Director IV Dionisio G. Alvindia.
 
This project is initiated by the Korea Agricultural Machinery Industry Cooperative (KAMICO), supported by South Korea’s Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs (MAFRA), the Korea Rural Community Corporation (KRC), and the Cabanatuan City Government, led by Myca Elizabeth R. Vergara.
 
Ambassador Sang-Hwa Lee, MAFRA Deputy Minister Jung Wook Kim, KRC Director Chan Won Choi, and KAMICO Chair Shin Gil Kim attended the groundbreaking event, highlighting South Korea's commitment to the initiative.
 
The complex will have a total development cost of $100 million, with $80 million provided by Korean investors and $20 million from the Government of the Philippines through the Department of Agriculture (DA) and the local government unit of Cabanatuan City.
 
Mayor Vergara noted last year that Cabanatuan is well-equipped to host the Agricultural Machinery Assembly Complex, as the city has access roads that can accommodate large trucks.
 
Director Alvindia stated that the goal of the KAMIC is to promote the local assembly and manufacturing of agricultural machinery and parts, supporting the government’s efforts to modernize the country’s agricultural sector.
 
Prior to the groundbreaking, PHilMech and its South Korean partners, MAFRA and KRC, held meetings to finalize the launch of the Agricultural Machinery Assembly Complex. The discussions focused on project operations, infrastructure requirements, and potential investments from Korean companies.
 
The delegation also identified opportunities to support the project with broader national needs, including provisions for irrigation and land rehabilitation efforts.

Marcos Jr. leads the ceremonial groundbreaking of the Korea Agricultural Machinery Industry Complex (KAMIC) in Barangay Kalikid Sur, Cabanatuan City, Nueva Ecija on December 10, 2025.

Established through a memorandum of understanding (MOU) between the Korea Agricultural Machinery Industry Cooperative (KAMICO) and the Department of Agriculture (DA), in collaboration with the local government unit (LGU) of Cabanatuan City, KAMIC is the first facility in the Philippines dedicated to the assembly and manufacturing of agricultural machinery, such as tractors, harvesters, cultivators and seeders, designed to meet local farming conditions.

It aims to enhance the country’s capacity to manufacture, fabricate, and assemble agricultural machinery and equipment; boost agricultural productivity and crop quality; increase farmers’ incomes; and provide farm machinery suited to Philippine requirements.

KAMIC will be built on a 20-hectare property owned by the local government in Barangay Kalikid Sur, a location jointly approved by the DA and the City Government of Cabanatuan. Construction is scheduled to start in 2026 and will last nine (9) years, carried out in three (3) phases: Semi Knock-Down (SKD) Assembly, Complete Knock-Down (CKD) Assembly and Full Manufacturing Assembly.

Aside from the groundbreaking ceremony, the Philippine Center for Postharvest Development and Mechanization (PhilMech) and DA-Central Luzon turn over agricultural machinery and equipment to 44 Farmer Cooperatives and Associations (FCAs).  Additionally, hybrid seeds and foliar inputs are distributed to support 22,103 hectares of hybrid rice for the 2025–2026 dry season cropping.

Since its inception in 1993, 367 programs from 235 local governments have been honored.

Rooted in the Department of Education’s commitment to nurturing environmental consciousness and cultural appreciation among learners, this initiative goes beyond a simple holiday activity. It serves as a gentle reminder that meaningful celebrations can also honor sustainability, responsibility, and love for our shared environment. The Christmas season, deeply woven into the heart of every Filipino, provides a beautiful opportunity for learners to reflect on the values of hope, generosity, and community. Through this contest, these values come alive in a tangible and creative way.

Using recycled, indigenous, and earth-friendly materials, participating schools will craft Christmas trees that not only symbolize the joy of the holidays but also tell stories of resourcefulness and resilience. Each entry is a testament to the students’ imagination and their ability to transform simple, everyday items into art that reflects Filipino culture and the vibrant spirit of the Banatu Festival.
